explanation: A function template in C++ allows the creation of a generic function that can operate with different data types without rewriting code for each type. When a function template is invoked, the compiler deduces the template parameters based on the function arguments, enabling type-safe, flexible, and reusable code. This feature is fundamental in generic programming, especially in the Standard Template Library (STL), where algorithms are designed to work with various container types and data.
syntax: template<typename T> void function_name(T& parameter); // or template<class T> void function_name(T& parameter);
example_explanation: This example defines a function template 'f' inside namespace 'N' that takes a reference to a parameter of any type T. When 'f' is called with an integer 'x' and a double 'y', the compiler deduces the template parameter T as 'int' and 'double' respectively. The function then prints the value, demonstrating how template functions enable generic, type-safe operations with automatic type deduction in modern C++.
